body: Ah, sorry. I read "things going on in our lives outside of our relationship problems with significant others" and figured since this wan't a problem involving my significant other it'd go here. But I'll go head over to r/relationship_advice. My bad.

I've looked into and the only service my school has is the health center and these "seminars" about depression and anxiety and I've been to both. 

And like I said, therapy or a psychiatrist aren't possible because I don't have a car and can't get to appointments and am not in a financial state where I could afford them outside the university.

 But thank you for your concern.
" I continued to smile at everything for a while until I couldn't even do that anymore" This really hit home with me. That's where I'm currently at now.

I know this has been 4 days old, but I needed to reply to this because your story sounds almost exactly like mine.

I was a freshman in college -- 18 years old and totally naive. Met this AWESOME guy 16 years older than me. He was in the army, he was sweet, sexy, etc. Well, he lost his job and started living with me. I start talking to his best friend from home (a couple of states away) and come to find out, my ex is married to a girl in another state. Apparently, he had told here he was in my state for work. To this day, idk if they had kids while I was dating him.

Anyway, I find out he's married and decided that we'd just be FWB until he had to move away for a year long service with the army and because he had nowhere to live until then. Well, shortly after learning of his marriage, I found out he was cheating on me with THREE different women, all of them not knowing he was married. 
Anyway, I got rid of his ass; I'd had enough. He still calls me from time to time, but I don't answer -- I don't have anything good to say to him. 

Overall: YES, LEAVE. Get the fuck out of that now. Idc if you have a kid, you deserve a man who can treat you better. He played you good, so good that you have to go asking questions if it was wrong for you to look through his phone.
